metadata.description: This graphs demonstrates how to use the transform data type to compute transforms as a connected chain rather than as isolated matrices. Consequently, each transform in the sequence inherits movements from its preceding parent transform.

_notes.text:
Use pivot and operator matrices. We use two nodes to demonstrate how transform chains should be handeled. **compute_transform_chain** compute transforms sequentially from the beginning to the end of the array. This approach treats the transforms as a connected chain rather than as isolated matrices. Consequently, each transform in the sequence inherits movements from its preceding parent transform.

If you set the value to *false*, **compute_transform** will compute each transforms as if they were isolated. The parent move inheritance will no longer be applied downstream, meaning that each transform operates independently of its parent.

Here we create a sequence of pivot matrices along the X axis.

We also create a single operator matrix to be used by all pivots. This operator matrix represents a rotation around the Y axis.

Use **transform_scope** to visualize a transform's world space coordinates directly within the viewport. This scope compound can accept either transforms or *4x4 matrix* data types as input.

When supplied with a transform type, the scope node will render the world matrix component. Alternatively, you can individually view other components of the transform by first decomposing it using the **access_transform_matrices** node.

_backdrops.title: Create sequence of world matrices to use as pivots
